subject: dec-database-state-store
text:
- **[Database / State Store] ndjson append logs + atomic JSON snapshots + std `File::lock` on separate `.lock` files (KEYSTONE).** Each event line is written with one `write` call. The next append heals a torn last line; readers count it and never rewrite the log. As landed (chunk 2026-10-10-self-healing-state): every appender (`append_event`, `append_event_at`, `try_append_event`) reads the log's last byte under the lock it already holds and, when the log is not empty and that byte is not LF, writes one LF and its line in a single write. The line then starts on a fresh line, no earlier byte moves, and every offset handed out before still starts the same line; `append_event_at` hands its builder and returns the offset its line really starts at (L + 1 after a heal, L otherwise). The healing process logs one `state-recovered` line, and an append that did not heal logs none. The one reader (`viola_state::events::read_from`: the wrapper's `wait` scan and `last` rebuild, `replay::session_chain`, the pass `viola revive` reads the logged session ids from, and since chunk 2026-10-10-session-links the wrapper's link-set restore at start, `LinkSet::restore`, one pass from offset 0, and since chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list `viola list`'s `viola_state::board::log_pass`, one pass from offset 0 per scanned instance whose snapshot read or was absent) counts what it steps over, per read, as `unknown_kinds`, `unknown_fields` and `torn_lines`: a line whose `kind` it does not know is not returned (`link` and `unlink` are known kinds since that chunk, returned and no longer counted); a known-kind line with a top-level key outside the six, or a `data` key outside its kind's list, is returned and counted once; an over-long line, a terminated line that is not one JSON object and the unterminated last line of the read count as torn, the last still neither returned nor rewritten.
 The counts are not logged. `viola list` is the first surface that shows them (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list): `list --json`'s `skipped` `{unknown_kinds, unknown_fields, torn_lines}` and the BAY line's `skipped a - b - c`, each summed over every scanned instance, gone ones included. The wheel is decided in the wrapper's memory and mirrored to a snapshot. Budget readings are timestamped, last-writer-wins, under `File::lock`. Rationale: the audit trail stays human-readable and `tail`-able, there is no C in the build, and there is no daemon to serialise writers. SQLite (C build, binary format) and redb (multi-process mode hardened only 2026-09-06) were rejected. Lock files are separate from logs because append + exclusive lock fails on Windows (rust-lang/rust#54118). Upgrade path if a real query need appears: a derived, rebuildable SQLite index (rusqlite) beside the authoritative log. The log stays the source of truth.

subject: dec-message-broker-ipc
text:
- **[Message Broker / IPC] interprocess 2.4.4 `local_socket`, one endpoint per `viola run`, behind viola's own `channel` seam.** `hook` blocks on the channel for a dialog answer. `wait` blocks until the next driver-relevant event (`turn-ended`, `question`, `permission`, `plan`, `session-end` or `dialog-expired`) and returns that event, so nothing polls and a driver parked in `wait` learns that a dialog is pending. If a dialog is already pending when `wait` is called without `after`, or with an `after` at or before that dialog's event line, it returns that dialog at once (as landed by 2026-10-04-dialog-answers-by-dialog-id: `hook.dialog` is served, the dialog line is appended and signalled through `WaitFeed::appending_dialog` and cleared through `WaitFeed::dialog_settled`). With an `after` past that line the driver has already seen the dialog, so `wait` blocks for the next driver-relevant event, and a driver that leaves a dialog to the human never spins. Each dialog event carries a wrapper-assigned `dialog_id` (an integer, monotonic per instance, with the counter restored from `events.ndjson` on start so an id never repeats across wrapper restarts), and `answer` names its target by that id. At most one dialog is pending per instance. A `hook.dialog` that arrives while another is pending is answered `null` at once, so that dialog renders for the human. Its event is still logged with its own `dialog_id`, and a later `answer` for it is refused `not-delivered` with detail `unknown-dialog`. Whether Claude Code can hold two dialog hooks open at once (for example on parallel tool calls) is a capability-ledger row. `wait` takes an optional `after` cursor and an optional `timeout_ms`. `after` is a byte offset into the instance's `events.ndjson`.
 `wait` returns the first driver-relevant event whose line starts at or after it, at once if that event is already logged, so a turn that ends before the driver calls `wait` is never missed. Every `send` `ok` payload and every `wait` event result carries `cursor`, the offset to pass as the next `after`. Without `after`, `wait` returns the next such event appended after the call. With no `timeout_ms` it blocks until an event arrives, and if the endpoint vanishes first the caller gets `instance-unreachable`. On timeout it returns `ok` with `{"timed_out":true}`. `last` returns the `last_assistant_message` of the newest `turn-ended` event. The wrapper holds it in memory and rebuilds it from `events.ndjson` on start. Endpoint names are a short hash of the instance, never the raw `VIOLA_NAME` + path. On Windows the client connects only through the SQOS Identification open (windows-sys `CreateFileW` with `SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT | SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION | FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED`, adopted by `Stream::try_from`), never interprocess's default connect, so a squatted or rogue server cannot impersonate the client; a non-overlapped handle adopted this way hangs (as measured at chunk 2026-09-25-security-prerequisites). Rationale: one API over named pipes and Unix sockets, sync and Tokio flavours, and no daemon. macOS caps socket paths at about 104 bytes. Accepted risk: interprocess has one main maintainer, which the seam contains.

subject: dec-hook-transport
text:
- **[Hook Transport] Exec-form `command` hooks: `"command": "<pinned viola copy>", "args": ["hook", "<event>"]`.** Tiers:
  - sync with a decision: PreToolUse with matcher `AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode`, plus PermissionRequest.
  - sync with no reply body (the ordering spine): SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop. Each writes its `hook.event` and exits 0 within viola's spine deadline: one built-in value for every event, below the `timeout` (5 s) those hooks get in `hooks.json`. That value is the product constant `viola_core::SPINE_DEADLINE` = 1 s, the bound the perf gate reads (test-plan §10). The connect deadline `viola hook` passes to `Client::connect_by` is the hook-local, crate-private `CONNECT_DEADLINE` = 750 ms (provisional), asserted below `SPINE_DEADLINE` by a unit test. If the endpoint cannot be reached or written within the deadline, the hook records the failure in `diagnostics/` and exits 0. The event is lost rather than the turn delayed, and a driver recovers through `wait`'s `timeout_ms`.
  - SessionEnd: sync within viola's own ~1 s budget: the channel under the same provisional 750 ms `CONNECT_DEADLINE`, else a direct `try_lock` append (`viola_state::try_append_event` with `Source::Hook`, which writes nothing while `events.ndjson.lock` is held), else nothing; `hooks.json` gives it no `timeout` key. `run` writes `session-end` from the process exit if no hook arrived.
  - `async: true`, printing nothing: Notification, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure.

  Rationale: exec form skips Git Bash path rewriting and shell startup. `http` hooks need a fixed URL, which means a central listener and so a daemon. `mcp_tool` is unavailable at SessionStart. The 1.5 s SessionEnd budget is never raised. The tier map is itself a ledger row that `viola verify` re-stamps.

subject: dec-hook-contract
text:
- **[Hook Contract] Hooks fail open.** Exit 0 with a JSON body is a decision. Exit 0 with no body is no decision (the `unverified-cli` degrade: the dialog renders for the human). Exit 2 is never produced. `hook` exits 0 at once when `VIOLA_NAME` is absent. The one exception is the hidden `hook <event> --capture <DIR> [--answers <DIR>]` arm, which only `viola verify`'s probe plugins call, and its statusline form `hook statusline --capture <DIR> [--shell <WORD>]`, which only Run B's probe settings call (it files the payload as `StatusLine.<k>.json` under the same claim and write, beside `StatusLine.<k>.shell` holding exactly `bin-sh` when the word equals `/bin/sh` byte for byte, else `other`, the word itself written nowhere; nothing printed; the founder's own answer to P4 fork 3 of chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows, «Run B + --settings», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I1`): it reads no `VIOLA_*`, does no obs init and opens no channel; it takes an absolute, existing `<DIR>`, reads stdin through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` and claims `<DIR>/<PascalEvent>.<k>.json` exclusively — create-new at 0600 (`viola_state::fs::create_private_new`) from the first free `k`, the next `k` on `AlreadyExists`, then the raw bytes through `replace_private` over its own claim, so two concurrent captures never share a name (`k` counts across events, so names sort in arrival order). `--answers <DIR>` is read only with `--capture` (inert without it): for a dialog event, the event's ordinal `j` in claim order selects `<DIR>/<Event>.<j>`, read through `take(64)` as an exact closed `ProbeAnswer` id, and `ledger::probe_body` builds the body from the filed payload through `dialog::decision_body` alone — one write to stdout, the probe's dialogs answered by the hook, never by a key.
 Any failure prints and writes nothing; stderr is always empty and the exit always 0 (the capture arm a boundary widening ratified live by the founder, 2026-09-28 20:24:32; its `--answers` body the founder's live ruling of 2026-10-05, relayed by the overseer). A sync dialog hook (`viola hook pre-tool-use|permission-request`) waits on `hook.dialog` for at most the instance's dialog hold, `config.json`'s `dialog_hold_s`: whole seconds from 60 to 3600, default 60 (`viola_core::DIALOG_HOLD_DEFAULT` · `DIALOG_HOLD_MIN` · `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX`, PROVISIONAL, beside `SPINE_DEADLINE`), a `DialogHold` read once at the wrapper's start; the hook bounds its reply read at the ceiling, `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX + 5 s` (3605 s), never at each start's hold, and writes stdout once. The dialog hooks' `timeout` in the embedded `hooks.json` is 3615 s, above the ceiling by a margin a test pins, so viola, never Claude Code, ends the wait, and the rendered plugin stays byte-identical across starts. At the hold's end the wrapper replies `null`: the hook exits 0 with no body and the dialog renders for the human. The wrapper then clears the pending `dialog_id`, and a later `answer` for it is refused `not-delivered` with detail `unknown-dialog`. `hook` never writes to stderr. Its codes-only process log goes to the home-level `diagnostics/hook-<name>.ndjson`, and content-bearing detail goes only to the instance's `diagnostics/detail-hook.ndjson` (format owned by obs). A failure to write either is ignored. Rationale: exit 2 is a blocking error in Claude Code's contract, and a viola bug must never block the user's session.

subject: dec-human-takeover-wheel
text:
- **[Human Takeover / Wheel] Byte-source claim + atomic send window + after-the-fact confirmation, explicit release.** Any human editing key since the last turn boundary moves the wheel to the human, and `send` is refused with `human-typing`. Only a closed non-editing list never counts (the founder's live ruling F-W2, 2026-10-04, relayed by the overseer): focus reports (`CSI I` / `CSI O`), mouse reports (X10 `CSI M` + 3 bytes, SGR `CSI < n;n;n M|m`, urxvt `CSI n;n;n M`) and terminal replies (DA1 `CSI ? … c`, DA2 `CSI > … c`, CPR `CSI n;n R`, DECRPM `CSI ? n;n $ y`, kitty flags `CSI ? n u`, OSC replies ending BEL or ST, DCS replies ending ST, and seven further reply shapes, each after `CSI` by exact grammar, the fields compared as bytes, no intermediate byte and the field count exact: DSR status `CSI 0 n`, colour scheme `CSI ? 997;1 n` and `CSI ? 997;2 n`, window size `CSI 4;n;n t`, cell size `CSI 6;n;n t`, text area `CSI 8;n;n t`, in-band resize `CSI 48;n;n;n;n t`, modifyOtherKeys reply `CSI > 4;n m`); a host resize is no stdin byte at all. The seven joined the list at chunk 2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive, ratified by the founder himself on 2026-10-08 after the exact grammars and a narrower option of two were shown (relayed verbatim by the overseer). As measured on foot 1.28.0 on the Linux dev host at that chunk (`evidence/terminal-replies.md`, `evidence/reply-probe.ndjson`, `evidence/reply-probe-fixed.ndjson`): before, those seven replies of the terminal were read as typing, and a live `claude` 2.1.287 took the wheel from the driver 237 ms after it started with no key typed; after, none of 23 probe queries is read as typing, and the nearest human keys (`n`, `t`, `m`, their Alt forms, their kitty key events) and a sequence one field or one prefix away from a listed shape still take the wheel.
 A reply no terminal has been measured to write is not added on a guess. Every other byte takes the wheel: ground bytes, every other completed sequence, a sequence past 64 bytes of parameters or payload, and a C0 inside a sequence (which aborts it). A read ending on a lone ESC is the Esc key at once, and a sequence past `ESC [` / `ESC ]` / `ESC P` / `CSI M` carries across reads. The classifier only observes: the stdin observer (`run::wheel::Observed`, wrapping the host stdin handed to `viola_pty::pump_with_paste`) returns every byte whole and unchanged, and a read holding an editing key moves the wheel before it returns.
 On Windows the platform decides what arrives (the founder's live ruling F-W3, 2026-10-04, relayed by the overseer): the inbox ConPTY outer terminal swallows focus reports, and under the sideloaded ConPTY's win32-input-mode request (`ESC[?9001h`) a mouse report written as text into the console's input arrives as one win32 key-down record per character (`ESC[0;0;<Uc>;1;0;1_`) and takes the wheel — as measured on `windows-2025` (ci#37227518624) for injected bytes; a mouse report from a real Windows terminal is not yet measured. The error only ever favours the human. A bridge send is written as one `ESC[200~…ESC[201~` + CR write. Human bytes arriving during that write are held in the pump and passed on straight after. An unsent `prompt-submitted` confirms and logs the take: one the hook filed `origin:"human"` moves the wheel before its line is appended (a `harness` prompt and the relabelled in-flight `driver` prompt never move it). An in-flight send whose text ends in CR or LF characters is typed without them, and one whose text holds a CR or a CR LF inside is typed with each as one LF, so its own prompt matches, is relabelled `driver` and moves no wheel (as landed at chunk 2026-10-07-a-send-ending-in-a-newline-is-confirmed for LF, at chunk 2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup for CR and CRLF at the end, and at chunk 2026-10-09-inner-cr-and-crlf-in-a-sent-text for a CR or a CR LF inside; [Delivery Confirmation]). A prompt that is not the in-flight send's typed text claims nothing and is appended as the hook filed it, so one filed `human` still moves the wheel.
 Harness-injected prompts are classified as harness turns, never as a human take: a prompt whose raw start (no trim) is one of `viola-agent-claude`'s four compiled `HARNESS_PREFIXES` — `<agent-message from=`, `<task-notification>`, `<\cross-session-message` or `<cross-session-message` (another Claude session's message; the unescaped form is the one measured from the CLI on 2.1.287, the escaped form is relayed and kept compiled, see Tag escaping). The side effect was accepted with the widening (the founder, live, 2026-09-29 15:21:44): a human who types the cross-session tag at a prompt's start is filed `harness`. As measured on 2.1.287, and not a new ratification, a human who types `<task-notification>` at a prompt's start is filed `harness` too. The wheel starts with `driver` when `viola run` starts, so automation is accepted until the first human editing key. A `send` while a turn is running (after `prompt-submitted`, before `turn-ended`) is not queued. It is refused `not-delivered` with detail `turn-running`, and the driver calls `wait` first. A `send` that arrives while another `send` is in flight (accepted, its outcome not yet recorded) is refused the same way, never queued, and nothing is typed for it. A `prompt-submitted` of any origin marks a turn running, and `turn-ended`, `session-start` or `session-end` ends it. A turn can end with no `turn-ended`: Claude Code's Stop hook does not fire on a user interrupt, and which hook, if any, fires for a turn that ends on an API error is a ledger row (if one does, `viola-agent-claude` registers it and maps it to `turn-ended` with a `null` `last_assistant_message`). A human interrupt is human input, so it moves the wheel to the human, and the `viola release` that returns the wheel clears the running-turn state.
 As built (as measured at chunk 2026-10-04-running-turn-refusal), the running-turn state lives in memory in `WheelSlot` beside the holder and cause, and records no event, snapshot field, span or obs line, so a restarted wrapper starts with no turn. The wrapper's one hook entry (`run::send::append_hook_event`) marks it before the hook's line is appended, keyed on the line's kind alone: a `prompt-submitted` of any origin (the claimed driver prompt included) marks it running, `turn-ended`, `session-start` or `session-end` ends it, and `activity` leaves it. So a driver that read `turn-ended` through `wait` is never refused by that turn. The turn is marked ahead of a human prompt's wheel move, so a `release` landing between the two still clears it. `send` reads the wheel and then the running turn twice, in that order both times: at the send's arrival, and again once the readiness gate's wait (up to `GATE_MAX_WAIT`, 8.5 s) has returned ready. A human key or a turn that started during the wait is refused `human-typing` or `not-delivered` / `turn-running`, with no `send-issued` and nothing typed (the overseer's technical answer of 2026-10-07T12:10Z at chunk 2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint, listed for the founder as a fact; it retires the residual recorded on 2026-10-04, under which a turn starting during the wait was not refused). The wait is not interrupted when the wheel moves: `Gate` knows nothing of the wheel, so the driver hears the refusal when the wait ends. Only a `release` that returns a human-held wheel clears the turn, in the same lock hold as the move. A `release` on a wheel the driver already holds, `release --budget` and a refused `release` (`release-from-driver`, invalid params) leave it, as do `pause` and human keys, so a turn left running under a driver-held wheel is recovered without a keystroke by `viola pause` then `viola release`.
 An unsent human prompt moves the wheel before its line is appended, so the `send` after it reads `human-typing`, never `turn-running`, and the `release` that returns the wheel also clears that turn. `release` never empties the in-flight `send` slot, which belongs to a live send. A SessionEnd the hook appends directly (the channel did not take it) leaves the turn marked — a recorded residual; its child is ending, so no driver `send` depends on it. A driver parked in `wait` across such a turn recovers through `timeout_ms`. CLI `viola pause` moves the wheel to the human without a keystroke, after which automated `send` is refused `human-typing` with detail `manual-pause`. The wheel returns only through CLI `viola release`; a `release` on a wheel the driver already holds changes nothing and appends nothing. The wheel lives in `src/run/wheel.rs` (`WheelSlot`: holder, cause and the running turn under one lock). The in-memory move is synchronous; each change's `wheel` event (`{holder, cause}`, `source:"wrapper"`, log-only, never through the wait feed), its snapshot update, its `run.wheel_transition` span and the pending-dialog hand-back run on the wheel's own worker thread, and `viola run` flushes that worker (bounded 2 s) at exit before the terminal leaves raw mode. Every snapshot write goes through the one in-process holder `src/run/snapshot.rs` (`Snapshots`). While the wheel is `human`, the wrapper answers `hook.dialog` with `null` at once, so the dialog renders for the human without waiting out the dialog hold, and `answer` is refused `human-typing`. If the wheel moves to the human while a `hook.dialog` is already pending (a human editing key or `viola pause`), the wrapper answers that pending request with `null` at once and clears its `dialog_id`, so a dialog held by the hook is never hidden from the human for the rest of the hold.
 `budget-paused` gates only `send`, never `hook.dialog` or `answer`, because a running turn finishes. Rationale: `viola run` owns the real stdin, so it knows byte provenance exactly. The prototype paused twice on harness turns before the classifier was fixed.

subject: dec-links
text:
- **[Links] A link `driver → driven` is recorded when a `send` or `answer` is issued from inside a wrapped session to another instance, or by an explicit `viola link <driver> <driven>`. `viola unlink` removes it.** A call counts as coming from inside a wrapped session when the calling process has `VIOLA_NAME` set. The CLI and the MCP server pass that name as `from` in the request `params`, and the driven instance's wrapper appends a `link` event to its `events.ndjson` only when that `driver → driven` pair is not already in its link set. Repeated sends and answers add no line, and an explicit `viola link` of an existing pair adds none and returns `{}`, so `since` is the time of the first link after any `unlink`. `unlink` appends an `unlink` event. Links are events in the log. The link set in the snapshot is derived by replaying them. Rationale: the log stays the single source of truth for the link set as it is for everything else. As landed (chunk 2026-10-10-session-links) only the implicit link is built. The driven wrapper's `LinkSet` (`src/run/links.rs`) records it on a `send` after the second wheel and running-turn reads and directly before `send-issued`, and on an `answer` once every refusal has passed and the response's kind matched the pending dialog, before the answer is taken. Five shapes of it stand on the operator's word and are not ruled by the founder: a refused `send` or `answer` records no link; a `from` equal to the wrapper's own name links nothing; the `link` line's `source` is `wrapper`; the record sits directly before `send-issued`, so a send that is issued and then reads `not-delivered` has linked; and a `link` line with no string `ts` reads `since: "unknown"`. A link that cannot be recorded is `-32603`, with nothing issued or the answer not taken. The set is restored from the log at every start.
 The explicit `viola link` / `viola unlink` and their two channel methods are not built: the wrapper answers `link` and `unlink` `-32601`, no subcommand exists, and no product path appends an `unlink` event (`LinkSet::remove` is unit-tested and has no caller). They are held: the boundary widening they carry is not ratified (the wrapper serving two more methods, the two verbs writing their frame after the liveness-only pre-check, and their snapshot read without the strict-modes check), and the founder's own answer of 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer, is that no explicit verb is built before Epoch 6, the three crossings staying unbuilt and unratified. The Epoch 6 working-route entry "Explicit session links", after "Windows endpoint admission" and "Server verification before any frame", carries the hold (moved there from the end of Epoch 5 by that answer; first moved from "The board: viola list" by the review card the founder approved, chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list).

subject: dec-session-liveness
text:
- **[Session Liveness] Heartbeat file primary; pid + process start time decide `gone`, and `claude agents --json` only enriches it.** Rationale: the prototype's heartbeat proved reliable. A bare pid is unsafe because pids get reused, which is why start time is matched too: a snapshot whose pid is dead, or alive with another start time, is `gone` whatever the heartbeat says (Session liveness). `claude agents --json` adds idle/busy status and shows unwrapped sessions as read-only rows. A `viola run` whose `ViolaName` is `live` or `stale` refuses to start (exit 1, with a message naming the instance); once the endpoint exists, a name with an answering endpoint refuses the same way. `viola revive` refuses a `live` or `stale` name through the same collision check and its two stderr pairs, as the first of its four preflight readings (the name's holder, the logged session, `session-live`, the recorded directory; a later reading is not taken once an earlier one refuses). `session-live` (chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board) is one `claude agents --json` read: a row whose `sessionId` is the logged id about to be resumed refuses, `--fork` skips the reading, and a failed read passes (fail open). As measured on 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host (that chunk's `evidence/live-p4.md`), a second interactive `claude --resume <id>` of an id a live `claude` holds is neither refused nor copied: both sessions run under the one id, two writers on one transcript, so the reading stays a refusal; and after `/clear` the agents row of the session's pid names the new id (P12 follows), so a session-id join survives a `/clear` because the wrapper rewrites the snapshot's `agent_session_id` on each `session-start`. The strict-modes check on the home and the instance's files runs ahead of them, before the wrapper log opens (chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor).
 A revive that passes goes through the same start as `run`, so the collision check runs twice. It resumes the `gone` instance in place: its `events.ndjson` is appended to with the earlier bytes unchanged, no launch is replayed, and its first record is `wheel{holder:"driver", cause:"start"}`, as every start's (the founder's answer, live, 2026-10-10, relayed by the operator: a revived start keeps the wheel at `driver`). Otherwise `run` starts in this order: program resolution (the `.cmd`/`.bat` refusal, which writes nothing), collision check, pinned copy and plugin folder, the ConPTY sideload (Windows x64, fail-open), version gate, exclusive bind of the endpoint (a bind that finds the name taken is an exit-1 refusal, `squatted-name`, so two concurrent starts cannot both win), first snapshot (with `endpoint`, `pinned_bin`, and `statusline_command` when the named source gave a command; `pid`, `started_at`) and heartbeat, the start `wheel` and `budget-gate` events, then the child spawn, after which the snapshot is rewritten with `child_pid`. Between the first snapshot and the spawn `run` also rewrites the per-session settings override (Unix only; §Occupied Resources, Claude Code integration names).
 As landed by 2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify every step has its place (the sideload step added by 2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty): program resolution → collision → pinned copy and plugin → ConPTY sideload (`run.conpty_sideload`, Windows: `pin_companions` + the absolute-path pre-load; `outcome` `loaded` · `hash-mismatch` · `unreadable` · `load-failed` · `not-built`, never a refusal; its held handles live until `spawn_child` returns) → strip plan → version gate (`run::version_gate`: the bounded `--version` read logged as a `version-probe` `process-start`/`process-exit` pair, the stamps read, `cli_version`/`cli_verified` carried into the first snapshot and the `claude-child` `process-start`; `run` prints nothing on any gate outcome) → endpoint bind → the budget gate at start (span `run.budget_eval` with `trigger: start`; it reads `budget.json`, restores no override and writes nothing; the thresholds were read from `config.json` earlier in the start, each rejection logged then) → first snapshot (its `budget_paused` is that verdict, its `budget_override_until` always absent) → heartbeat → start events (record two, `budget-gate`, carries that verdict's `data`, where it carried the constant `{"paused": false}` before chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor) → spawn, so the child's first SessionStart hook finds a listening endpoint and a recorded snapshot. Since chunk 2026-10-10-session-links the start also restores the wrapper's link set before the endpoint serves: it reads `events.ndjson` twice there (`WaitFeed::rebuild`, then `LinkSet::restore`), the first snapshot's `links` is the restored set, the start appends no line for links and its start records are unchanged. `viola revive` starts through the same function, so a revived start's first snapshot carries the logged links.
 A gone instance's directory is reused at once, and its `events.ndjson` is appended to, never truncated.

subject: conv-exit-codes
text:
- **CLI exit codes:**
  - `0` ok
  - `1` internal error (anyhow edge), `viola run` refusing to start because its `ViolaName` is `live` or `stale` ([Session Liveness]; `detail:"already-live"`, stderr `unable: <name> is already live` / `hint: viola list`, or `unable: <name> is still running but not answering` with the stale hint), `viola run` refusing a pinned copy that fails its re-hash (`detail:"pinned-hash-mismatch"`, `unable: the pinned viola copy failed its integrity check`), `viola run` refusing a `.cmd`/`.bat` child program before any spawn (`process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"batch-script-child"}`, the two fixed `unable:`/`hint:` stderr lines), and `viola run` losing the exclusive endpoint bind to another holder (`detail:"squatted-name"`, `unable: the endpoint for <name> is held by another process` / `hint: another process holds this name's endpoint; stop it or pick another name`, no path, pid or pipe name); `viola revive` refusing its strict-modes check, which runs before the wrapper log opens and outside the preflight (`unable: <name>'s state files can be written by another user` and its `hint:` on stderr, exit 1, no log opened and no line written, on the start arm as on `--list`; chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor), and `viola revive` refusing at its preflight, whose four readings (the name's holder, the logged session, `session-live`, the recorded directory;
 chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board added the third) are taken in a fixed order and stop at the first refusal: `detail:"already-live"` (`run`'s own collision check and its two pairs, unchanged), `detail:"no-session"` (two pairs: `unable: <name> has no logged session to resume`, and `unable: <name> has no logged session with that id` for an `--id` the log does not hold), `detail:"session-live"` (`unable: <name>'s session is open in another claude` / `hint: close it there first, or start a copy: viola revive <name> --fork`, the founder's wording, his own answer to P4 fork 4 of chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board, `inputs#I1`; one `claude agents --json` read lists the logged id live in another `claude`; skipped under `--fork`; a failed read passes) and `detail:"cwd-missing"` (`unable: <name>'s recorded directory is missing`), each one `unable:` / `hint:` pair on stderr that holds no recorded directory, pid or logged id and one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail}` in `run-<name>.ndjson`; under `--json` each of these revive refusals, the strict-modes one included, is instead one stdout document `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` (`strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing`; `client::refused_document`) with stderr empty, the same exit 1 and the same log lines, while a refusal `run`'s start makes after a passed preflight prints no document (owed to "Exit-cause code catalogue"; chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract) (`viola revive --list` has two refusals: the strict-modes check, the stderr pair or its document and exit 1 with no log line, and `no-session`, the stderr pair or its document and exit 1 with, under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME`, `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"no-session"}` in the caller's `cli-<VIOLA_NAME>.ndjson`);
 `viola verify` with a failing ledger row (its stamp still written, last stdout line `stamped <ver>  <n> pass  <m> fail`), `viola verify` stopped by Ctrl-C or TERM before its rows are checked (no stamp written, stdout empty, stderr exactly `unable: verify was stopped before it finished` / `hint: run viola verify again to stamp this CLI`, and `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"interrupted"}` when `VIOLA_NAME` holds a valid name; chunk 2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup) and verify's refusals, each an `unable:` + `hint:` pair on stderr with no path: `the claude CLI was not found` / `install Claude Code or put it on PATH`, `the claude CLI is a .cmd or .bat script` / `pass the real executable, not a .cmd or .bat shim`, `the CLI version could not be read` / `run claude --version to check the install`, `a recorded fixture is not clean: <file> <code>` (a screen: `<file> row <n>[ seam] <code>`; codes `home-path` · `absolute-path` · `username` · `email`; never the content) / `record with a viola home under your user home`, plus run's pinned-copy re-hash refusal; and the `cli` role's internal error: `src/main.rs` `role_of` files every first word but `run`, `revive`, `mcp`, `hook` and a leading `-` flag under `cli` (a first word `mcp`, after any `--home <dir>` / `--home=<dir>`, is `Role::Mcp`, whose exit maps like `Other` and which never prints `error: internal error` — `prints_internal_error` stays `Cli`-only; chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers), and `revive` followed (after any `--home` pair) by `--list` before a `--` under `cli` too (every other `revive` is a wrapper beside `run`, and its start arm logs as process `run`; a `--list` after `--` is the child's word;
 so `send`, `wait`, `last`, `list`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `verify`, `revive --list` and `plugin install`), and a dispatch `Err` or a caught panic in any of them prints exactly `error: internal error` on stderr once, from the `main` catch site, no hint — no dispatch arm prints it; for `viola wait` / `viola last` exit 1 also covers a refusal reply, a reply of no known shape, and any channel error but a failed connect or a closed / reset connection (those are exit 21); for `viola list` exit 1 covers an `instances/` that exists and cannot be listed (or an entry whose type cannot be read) and a log start that fails, while a per-instance read error gives no row (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list)
  - `2` usage error (clap, a second positional to `viola send` included; never produced by `viola hook`), and `viola send` text over `MAX_FRAME` or not UTF-8 (`error: the text must be readable UTF-8 of at most 16 MiB`)
  - `10` `human-typing`
  - `11` `budget-paused`
  - `12` `unverified-cli`
  - `13` `not-delivered`
  - `14` `unknown` refusal
  - `20` protocol fault from the wrapper
  - `21` instance unreachable (no live endpoint for the `ViolaName`); also `viola list`'s refused strict-modes check of the home, `instances/` or any one instance, which refuses the whole board (`--json` `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":null}`, no log opened) — the founder's own answer, 2026-10-13, relayed verbatim by the Viola overseer (the operator's answer at chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list's planning, superseded 2026-10-13); `viola plugin install`'s refused strict-modes check of the home or an existing `marketplace/` tree dir is the same exit and document (human mode the home-state pair; nothing created, no log opened)

subject: conv-mcp-results
text:
- **MCP:** a success is a tool result with `isError: false` and the channel `ok` payload as `structuredContent` (for `list`, the caller-side `{items, budget, skipped}` payload, the `list` payload of Standard Contracts). A refusal is a tool result with `isError: true` and the same `refusal` + `detail` in `structuredContent`. An unreachable instance and a wrapper protocol fault are also `isError: true` tool results. Their `structuredContent` is `{"error":"instance-unreachable"|"wrapper-fault","detail":…}`, the same as CLI `--json` (`instance-unreachable` with `detail: null`; `wrapper-fault` with the JSON-RPC fault's `{code,message,data}`). As landed (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers): each handler re-validates its raw argument object (`target` through `ViolaName::try_new`, `text` a string, `after` / `timeout_ms` absent, `null` or a `u64`, `dialog_id` a `u64`, `response` an object through `Response::parse`), and a failure is an `isError: true` result `{"error":"invalid-params","detail":"<field>"}` (the closed field words `target` · `text` · `after` · `timeout_ms` · `dialog_id` · `response`) with no frame written; every `isError` text is `refused: <code>`. JSON-RPC errors are the MCP connection's own faults, an unknown tool name (`-32602`) and an internal handler fault — any other channel error, a reply of no known shape, a `wait` / `last` refusal, a panicked call — which is `-32603` `internal error` with `data: null`. `tools/list`'s result carries `ttlMs` 0 and `cacheScope` `private`: claude 2.1.287 negotiates protocol `2026-07-28` and drops every tool of a list result without them (as measured live at that chunk, `evidence/live-mcp.md` start 1).
 claude 2.1.302 on that protocol opens with `server/discover` (its JSON-RPC id a string) and then `tools/list`, each carrying `_meta` (`io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion`, `…/clientInfo`, `…/clientCapabilities`), and sends no `initialize` or `notifications/initialized`; viola's two results each carry `ttlMs` 0 and `cacheScope` `private` (as measured live at `viola-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup-ii/evidence/live-tap.md`, start 2). That recorded exchange, `fixtures/claude/2.1.302/Mcp.tools-list-1.json`, is replayed against `viola mcp` by `tests/mcp_recorded_exchange.rs` (`viola-e2e`), which takes the `tools/list` response by its request's id and holds the served result to the recorded result's key and type shape, its tool names in order.

subject: contract-snapshot-envelope
text:
**Snapshot envelope** (atomically replaced JSON)
```json
{"v":1,"written_at":"2026-09-23T19:43:58.123Z","writer":"0.1.0","data":{}}
```
A snapshot whose `v` is higher than the reader supports, or that fails to parse, is ignored, and the state is rebuilt by replaying `events.ndjson`. Replay recovers only log-derived fields: `links`, `agent_session_id`, `wheel`, `budget_paused` and `budget_override_until`. Fields no event carries (`endpoint`, `pid`, `started_at`, `pinned_bin`, `statusline_command`, `cli_version`, `cli_verified`, `child_pid`, `pending_dialog`, `cwd`) are treated as absent. Liveness then rests on the heartbeat alone, so the instance is `live` or gone and never `stale`. The endpoint is rebuilt as described under IPC endpoints, and `hook statusline` prints nothing. As landed the fallback is library code in `viola-state` with two product readers, each after `viola_state::strict::check_instance` has passed: `viola revive`'s preflight takes it in its second reading, the logged session (chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive; second of four since chunk 2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board added `session-live`, the strict-modes check ahead of the preflight since chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor), and `viola list`'s `viola_state::board::read` (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list), which gives a `list` payload item for a replayed snapshot only when the beat is at most `STALE_AFTER` (5 s) old: `live`, never `stale`, `dialog_pending: false`, no CLI field, `wheel` / `budget_paused` only where the log gave one; an absent snapshot or a failed replay gives no item. `snapshot::read_snapshot_classified` tells four cases apart through the same `MAX_FRAME` bound: the snapshot, no file, an unreadable one, and an unsupported one with the `v` it saw. It reads the envelope's `v` first: above 1 is unsupported whatever else the envelope holds, 1 must then parse whole, and anything else (a `v` of 0 included) is unreadable.
 `replay::read_snapshot_or_replay` replays the log for an unreadable or unsupported snapshot, in one pass, and logs one `state-recovered` line; an absent snapshot is neither replayed nor logged, and the replay writes no file. It recovers `wheel` and the budget gate from their last line and `agent_session_id` from the last `session-start` that carries one; a field no line gave is absent, never a default; `links` is recovered in the same pass through the public rule `viola_state::replay::apply_link_line` (chunk 2026-10-10-session-links): a `link` line whose `data.driver` and `data.driven` are strings adds `{driver, driven, since}` with `since` that line's `ts` unless the set holds the pair, an `unlink` line removes the pair, and a line of another kind or with a name that is no string changes nothing. A `link` line with no string `ts` gets `since: "unknown"`, the form `session_chain` takes for a missing `ts`; no writer of this build makes such a line, and the shape stands on the operator's word, the founder not having ruled on it. `read_snapshot` keeps its results, and its five product callers (`src/cmd/client.rs`, `run`'s collision check, `src/cmd/hook.rs` twice, `src/cmd/hook/statusline.rs`; the rule: `read_snapshot(` under `src/`, outside test modules) still read every such snapshot as absent. A replayed snapshot gives no `cwd`, so a revive over one is refused `cwd-missing`. Beside the replay, `replay::session_chain` reads the logged sessions for revive in one pass over `events.ndjson` through `events::read_from`: one link per `session-start` line whose `agent_session_id` is a string, with the pass's skip counts. It writes and logs nothing.

subject: contract-channel-methods
text: - `send` `{text, from?}` → `{submitted_at, cursor}` when confirmed, or `{confirmed:false, detail:"unconfirmable", cursor}`. `cursor` is the end offset of `events.ndjson` when the send was accepted, before the paste. A `send` reads the wrapper's budget gate once at its arrival ([Budget Governor]); a closed gate is the refusal `budget-paused` with detail `five-hour` or `seven-day`, before `send-issued`, with no cursor, nothing typed and no flight reserved, and a gate change that cannot be recorded there answers `-32603`. Since chunk 2026-10-10-session-links a `send` whose `from` is a name other than the wrapper's own records the link `from → this instance` ([Links]) after the second wheel and running-turn reads and directly before `send-issued`: a new pair's `link` line stands directly before that send's `send-issued`, whose `cursor` is still the offset its own line starts at, and a pair the set holds adds nothing. A link that cannot be recorded answers `-32603` with nothing issued and nothing typed. A send refused at an earlier rung, one with no `from` and one whose `from` is the wrapper's own name record nothing.

subject: contract-channel-methods
text: - `wait` `{after?, timeout_ms?, from?}` → `{event:<ndjson event line>, cursor}`, where `cursor` is the end offset of that event's line, or `{timed_out:true}`. `after` and `timeout_ms` are each absent or a non-negative integer that fits `u64` (`null`, a negative, a fraction or a string is `-32602`, `data: null`); unknown fields are ignored. The start offset is `after`, else `events.ndjson`'s end read at the call; a line counts only when it STARTS at or after it. A pending dialog comes first: an `after`-less `wait`, or one whose `after` is at or before the pending dialog's line, returns that dialog at once. Only `turn-ended` · `question` · `permission` · `plan` · `session-end` · `dialog-expired` wake (`viola_core::EventKind::WAIT_WAKE`); the deadline is `now + timeout_ms` through `Instant::checked_add` (an unrepresentable instant is no deadline). The wake (`src/run/wait.rs` `WaitFeed`): one `Mutex` (a generation counter + the newest turn) and one `Condvar`; `WaitFeed::appending` runs each hook line's append inside the lock, then bumps the generation, keeps a `turn-ended` as the newest turn and wakes the parked calls. Hook lines signal, and of the wrapper's own records only `dialog-expired`, appended through `WaitFeed::appending` (the wrapper's `send-*`, `link` and start records never wake). A parked `wait` reads the generation before each scan, re-scans only when it moves, and its 20 ms `wait_timeout` re-reads the injected clock against the deadline, never the file; it holds its connection's worker thread until a wake, its deadline or the wrapper's exit.

subject: contract-channel-methods
text: - `hook.event`, sent id-less by `hook` (a notification, no reply): `{ts, event:{kind, data}}`. The wrapper re-validates the event (`kind` is one of the five hook kinds `session-start` · `prompt-submitted` · `turn-ended` · `session-end` · `activity`; `data` is an object; for `prompt-submitted`, `text` is a string and `origin` is `harness` · `human`) and appends `{v, ts:<append time>, instance, kind, source:"hook", data}` to `events.ndjson`. An invalid event is not appended, and an append failure is `-32603`. A `prompt-submitted` whose `text` exactly equals the in-flight `send`'s typed text (the sent text with every CR LF pair and every other CR as one LF, and without its trailing CR and LF characters; any `origin` the hook filed) is appended with `origin:"driver"` instead, and only then settles that send ([Delivery Confirmation]). The one in-flight send no `prompt-submitted` claims is a listed local command waiting for its post-condition: a `session-start` whose `cause` is `clear` and whose `agent_session_id` is a string differing from the remembered one is appended unchanged and only then settles it.

subject: res-filesystem
res-filesystem
text: - Test-only, outside the viola home: `<temp dir>/viola-root-watch/<test name, :: → .>.<label>.report` — the root test support `tests/support/watch.rs` `Watch` (bound `WITHIN` = 7 s, shared by the root waits on a child: `Instant::now() + WITHIN` reads 28 sites in 20 files under `tests/`, as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor's wrap on the Linux dev host's final tree (two more than at chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive: one each in `tests/cli_budget.rs`, a new file, and `tests/cli_revive.rs`), the shared `tests/support/events.rs` and `tests/support/cli.rs` holding one each; that pattern is the count's rule and not a census of every wait on the bound. One of the waits is `tests/support/home.rs` `wait_endpoint_gone`, which `Wrapper::stop` / `stop_keep` run after the wrapper's exit until the snapshot's recorded `endpoint` is unconnectable; after a kill, `Wrapper::kill` waits on `holder_gone` instead (on Unix a connect to the path is refused or the path is absent, on Windows the pipe is not found), because a killed wrapper removes nothing and its socket file stays on Unix, where the stop path's rule is the file being absent (as measured at chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive, the kill-and-revive case green on the three CI runners)). It is created empty at the wait's start and gets a line only when the polled state changes (codes, counts and booleans only), so a test the runner kills keeps its evidence. It is kept when the test panics or is killed and removed when it passes. `viola` never reads or writes it.
